models.provenance: Hashes computed from the files qualified by ear, which came from the thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx GitHub release model-files-v1.0. Byte-identity with the pinned source was verified against the Hugging Face API: at the pinned revision, both files' LFS SHA-256s match these hashes exactly. Voices are the American and British English presets in voices-v1.0.bin that pass curation's artifact checks, minus am_adam, which the author grades F+ in Kokoro-82M's VOICES.md; fourteen more presets were refused for crackle, clipping or high-frequency noise on the standard passage, bm_lewis among them once he was phonemized in his own English; a Voice is qualified for Simple only if that grading gives it B- or better and the curator approved its recipe by ear.

models.provenance: mlx-community's 8-bit MLX conversion of ResembleAI/chatterbox-turbo (350M parameters, MIT), pinned at its current revision. 8-bit rather than 4-bit because a 350M model loses more to 4-bit than the 0.6B Qwen3 does, and its 706MB weights are still well inside the 8GB floor. Peak resident memory measured 0.88GB during offline narration, placing it in the 1GB RAM class. Neither upstream nor the conversion ships a LICENSE file beside the weights. The converter's apache-2.0 card tag conflicts with Resemble AI's explicit MIT release of the Turbo weights; Readily follows the model owner's terms and immutable holder notice.

models.provenance: Curated from supertone-oss-archive/supertonic-2, where Supertone moved the repository, at the pinned revision; its files are byte-identical to Supertone/supertonic-2 at 75e67276, and hashed from the bytes the curation script downloaded. The loader directly runs upstream's four ONNX graphs with no added runtime dependency or download path. Peak resident memory measured 0.90GB during ten-Voice offline qualification, placing it in the 1GB RAM class; all four graphs were inspected and contain no random operators. Version 3 re-curates the same weights after the loader began trimming the vocoder output to its predicted duration and dropping characters the indexer does not know, so audio narrated by version 2 never mixes with it.

models.name: supertonic
models.provenance: Curated from supertone-oss-archive/supertonic-3, where Supertone moved the repository, at the pinned revision; its files are byte-identical to Supertone/supertonic-3 at 3cadd1ee, and hashed from the bytes the curation script downloaded. Its export keeps Supertonic 2's four-graph layout, JSON sidecars and voice style format, so it loads through the same supertonic Architecture with no added dependency or download path. Its LICENSE is byte-identical to Supertonic 2's BigScience OpenRAIL-M. The F3 preset is left out: it scores 0.07 to 0.15, with the audio trimmed to its predicted duration, on check A's hf8k ratio against the 0.05 limit on every Segment of the standard passage. Peak resident memory measured 1.07GB across the whole nine-Voice curation run, download and capture included, placing it in the 1GB RAM class.

models.name: vibevoice-realtime
models.provenance: mlx-community's 8-bit MLX conversion of microsoft/VibeVoice-Realtime-0.5B (MIT), pinned at its current revision. The licence is MIT and carries no use restriction; Microsoft's model card recommends the model for research and development, asks that listeners be told the speech is AI-generated, and rules out impersonation, disinformation and live voice conversion, none of which narrating a reader's own text is. Microsoft's own release adds an audible disclaimer and a watermark that this conversion does not carry. Upstream's generation defaults are kept: guidance 1.5 and 5 diffusion steps, as in its realtime demo. The model takes no voice reference; its preset Voices are the prefilled prompt caches the checkpoint ships under voices/, and only the English ones are listed because upstream supports English speech only. The en-Grace_woman preset is left out: it scores 0.0548 on check A's hf8k ratio against the 0.05 limit on one Segment of the standard passage. mlx-audio's loader fetches the Qwen2.5 tokenizer from the Hub, so the Engine bundles that tokenizer, pinned by hash, and never makes the fetch. Peak resident memory measured 1.23GB across the whole six-Voice curation run, download and capture included, placing it in the 2GB RAM class.

Every Block is cloned the Hi-Fi way upstream recommends, from the Voice's bundled reference clip and continuing from that clip and its transcript, the clip resampled to the audio VAE's 16 kHz by the Engine's own polyphase filter instead of mlx-audio's SciPy path. One Block measured 6.2GB MLX peak on an M1 Pro, placing it in the 6GB class.

support_models.name: wav2vec2
support_models.provenance: ONNX community conversion of facebook/wav2vec2-base-960h, whose publisher declares Apache-2.0 at https://huggingface.co/facebook/wav2vec2-base-960h. Conversion model card names that base_model; no separate licence or NOTICE is shipped by the conversion. Readily supplies Apache-2.0 terms. FP32 graph, 32-label HF vocabulary and waveform normalization retained together. Anonymous download, SHA-256 verification and CPU ONNX inference tested. This is the HF distribution, not the MIT TorchAudio bundle.
